channel.title: AI News Radar
channel.description: A curated 24-hour radar of AI news: official releases, new models and high-signal discussion.

item.title: nemotron-halloween
item.description: MonsterHouse, a Halloween interactive projection on NVIDIA Nemotron Voice Agent, hears trick-or-treaters, replies as a grumpy pirate ship, softens at please, and runs on one workstation using Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB after testing over a dozen models. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: US tech stocks see sharp falls over AI cost fears
item.description: Intel’s one-day fall of as much as 30%, Nasdaq’s over-3.5% drop and more than $500 billion erased from Alphabet’s market value show AI spending fears driving a second straight tech selloff.

item.title: Making it easier for websites to express AI training preferences
item.description: OpenAI will honor a shared robots.txt signal so website operators can communicate AI training preferences to multiple participating providers at once and avoid maintaining separate crawler rules, with implementation planned in the coming months. (OpenAI News)

item.title: “Black October” for AI Developer Platforms
item.description: Wiz documented at least nine AI developer platforms—including Fireworks AI, Lightning AI, Railway, Warp and OpenCode—hit by October security incidents tied to credential theft, agent swarm attacks, distillation-motivated theft and LLMJacking, with roughly $371,000 in cryptocurrency stolen.

item.title: Alibaba partners with Apple to integrate Qwen into Apple Intelligence, with testing opening November 4
item.description: Alibaba and Apple will integrate Qwen into Apple Intelligence, letting Chinese users call Qwen's text and image understanding and content generation from Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence, with developer beta testing from November 4 and a full iOS 27.3 release in December, opt-in only and with requests and replies excluded from model training.

item.title: Cracks are emerging in the AI spending boom
item.description: Big Tech is pouring billions into AI infrastructure while mounting debt, negative cash flow and growing investor skepticism raise questions about whether the AI spending boom can be sustained.

item.title: Community safety report and new protections for teens
item.description: OpenAI says it referred over 200 ChatGPT-related potential violent threats to law enforcement in Q3 2026, will publish its first safety report in early 2027 and update it semiannually, and has tightened firearm-content limits for minors. (OpenAI News)

item.title: Anthropic IPO filing reveals nearly $900 billion in hidden debt
item.description: Anthropic's IPO filing reveals nearly $900 billion in planned debt for servers, buildings and power, against $117.5 billion of balance-sheet liabilities and $112 billion in cash, with off-balance-sheet obligations worrying Wall Street.

item.title: Google's AI Mode doesn't drive traffic "for anybody," Reddit CEO Huffman warns the entire web
item.description: Reddit lost more than 1 million weekly Google search referrals in October and its stock fell over 25% despite strong earnings, as CEO Steve Huffman said AI Mode drives no traffic and warned every business relying on search traffic.

item.title: Silicon Valley wants you to invest in miracles
item.description: Anthropic's 335-page S-1 pairs a founder letter promising an age of miracles with 94 pages of risk factors warning its models could pose catastrophic or even existential risks to humanity, as The Verge examines Silicon Valley's pitch to Wall Street.

item.title: How to Build Your Own Always-On AI Agent
item.description: OpenRouter's tutorial builds an always-on TypeScript agent with @openrouter/agent 0.11.0 that polls Hacker News, remembers read items across restarts, and costs $0.0003–$0.0012 per check, stopping each run at five cents.

item.title: Nvidia weighs playing the cosigner for Nscale’s AI data center in West Virginia
item.description: Nvidia is in talks to cosign billions of dollars in debt financing for Nscale's West Virginia AI data center built for Anthropic, which has already signed a $44.6 billion contract for the first building.

item.title: AI can turn public security fixes into working exploits before users receive an update
item.description: Epoch AI found Z.ai's GLM 5.3 used about $1,000 of compute to reverse-engineer Mozilla's published-but-unshipped Firefox patches into web attacks in as little as 12 hours, breaking all six versions released September 17 to October 26 and reading visitors' files.

item.title: The TL;DR on Figma Weave: Make your creative process repeatable
item.description: Figma Weave links AI image and video generation and editing nodes into reusable workflows, lets teams branch from one backpack photo to compare prompts and models, and packages workflows as one-click Weave tools for teammates. (Figma AI / Agent / Make)

item.title: This incredible. Gemma 4 became the first LLM to run in space?
item.description: Google's Project Suncatcher reportedly sent commands to a prototype satellite, booted a TPU in orbit and received a haiku from Gemma 4, which Philipp Schmid calls the first LLM run in space — though the post offers few verification details.

item.title: Ultrathink
item.description: Anthropic renamed its Claude subscription tiers so Max 5x becomes Max and Max 20x becomes Ultra, with prices unchanged at $100 and $200 per month, while most existing verified Ultra accounts lose the 5-hour usage limit and new accounts keep a temporary cap to prevent fraud, though weekly limits stay the same.

item.title: AI Can Rearrange and Cover Songs Too? Spotify Plans Paid Music Remixing Service
item.description: Spotify plans to launch an AI remix service in the first quarter of 2027 letting paid subscribers rearrange or cover songs for roughly $4 to $5 a month, under licensing deals with Universal Music Group and two other labels. (AIbase)

item.title: Fable 5.5 tests reveal: behind every Claude response, an invisible “safety trial” is quietly running
item.description: Test feedback on Anthropic's Fable5.5 (or Opus5.5) shows it fixing bugs and tracing underlying architecture risks in coding tests, while the piece dissects a Self-Assessment mechanism that runs a hidden review after each Claude answer. (AIbase)

item.title: Anthropic expected to receive high ‘junk’ rating from credit agencies following IPO, FT report says
item.description: Anthropic is expected to receive a high junk credit rating from rating agencies after its IPO, per the FT, a Blackstone forecast that would make fundraising harder and costlier for its massive spending. (TechCrunch AI)

item.title: Meta turns your social feed into a fitting room: Style Sketch lets old photos spawn an AI stylist
item.description: Meta’s free Style Sketch links Facebook and Instagram to identify clothes in old photos for a virtual wardrobe and generates outfits by body type and skin tone plus weather- or trip-based packing lists, but only in Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand. (AIbase)
